pcs.pc_description: Analyse the current trends, latest technologies or updates in the market by extracting key facts from formal and informal sources.
Engage actively in forums and discussions to stay informed about any changes in industry practices and developments.
Stay current with relevant laws and regulations that may affect the organisation.
Compare the various elements with the current services provided by the organisation.
Classify the value-added services that can be offered and propose them to management with details on how they can create an impact.
Evaluate new market opportunities and determine how they can be leveraged for the organisation’s benefit.
Identify competitors, their key clients, and how their activities are evolving.
Maintain constant familiarisation of service offerings and developments in the organisation and the industry.

modules.module_title: Prepare and implement a sales plan for acquiring new clients

pcs.pc_description: Develop a sales plan and other business development initiatives.
Obtain relevant data/information from the organisation’s internal knowledge base, CRM database, and other sources (social media, email, content marketing, etc.).
Review the data and generate a list of prospective clients.
Contact leads using appropriate modes of communication and at frequencies specified in the sales plan.
Analyse the lead characteristics and devise customised strategies for lead conversion.
Record new business development activities and lead responses on the CRM database.

Contribute strategic information to the regional/national sales team, including key results from previous calls, updates on current target accounts and a review of the following week’s key upcoming calls.
Keep track of daily sales development and relationship-building activities.
Prioritise the customers for contact based on the possibility of lead conversion.
Contact customers to fix up appointments for in-person meetings.
Give a brief explanation of the company and its offerings to the customer.
Enquire about customers’ requirements and analyse the best courier service offering possible.
Recommend services with features and explain the benefits.
Provide data-driven insights like shipping trends, efficiency improvements, and cost savings.
Demonstrate technical advantages such as easy-to-use online booking systems, automated alerts, inventory management integration, API integration with their systems for real-time data flow, etc.
Highlight if any eco-friendly practices are offered, such as green logistics, electric vehicles, or carbonneutral deliveries.
Showcase success stories or testimonials from similar clients in their industry to build credibility.
Propose customised courier services packages that align with customer needs and costs and send a formal proposal.
Consider offering discounted or free trials for certain services, such as express delivery, free pickup service, or real-time tracking for a limited time.
Perform effective negotiation, if required, with terms such as Cost, Contract length, Payment terms, Contract volume, VAS, Delivery/implementation timing, etc.
Request the customer to give adequate time to inquire with the Key Accounts sales manager about a revised service cost and payment terms if negotiation fails.
Use persuasive techniques to encourage leads to make a purchase decision.
Implement lead conversion strategy in a timed manner.
Perform contract management after the lead is converted.
Collect payment details of customers/organisations.
Follow up after the sale to ensure satisfaction, encourage repeat business, and ask for referrals.
Record new business development activities and lead responses on the CRM database.

pcs.pc_description: Obtain a list of existing clients assigned by the Key Account Manager.
Prioritise the clients for contact based on the previous relationship-building calls made to each of them.
Meet with the clients in person and inquire about their goals, challenges, and feedback on current services offered.
Irrespective of the outcome, take note of the client’s feedback before leaving.
Stay in touch with clients regularly through calls, emails, or meetings and adapt to clients’ schedules and preferred communication methods.
Appreciate customers’ continued business through thank-you emails, special offers, or gestures like personalised gifts or loyalty rewards.
Suggest complementary services, upgrades, or new shipping solutions that could enhance the client’s experience or help them achieve their goals.
Offer valuable insights into market trends, industry developments, or new technologies that may impact their business.
Regularly ask clients for feedback on your products, services, and overall performance.
Create loyalty programs or incentives for long-term clients to encourage repeat business and foster deeper relationships.
Offer clients exclusive invites to webinars, product launches, or industry events where they can network and learn.
Use CRM tools to track client interactions, purchase history, preferences, and key milestones.

Measure and assess client satisfaction regularly using Net Promoter Scores (NPS), customer satisfaction surveys, customer retention rate, churn rate, or other metrics to gauge the relationship’s health.
Offer training or resources to help the client utilise services.
Ensure that the existing contracts meet specific business needs, offering customised pricing, service levels, or delivery terms.
Address any change in scope or pricing through formal amendments to the contract.
Check the expiry of existing contracts and arrange for the renewal process.
Initiate negotiations, if applicable, well before the contract expires, review terms, adjust pricing, and update if any new elements.
Ensure the termination process is smooth if the contract is not renewed and the client receives any required final deliverables or support.

pcs.pc_description: Act as the customer’s primary point of contact and value the client’s preferences, needs, and goals.

Offer 24/7 support for key clients through various means, such as real-time tracking notifications, proactive alerts, a helpline number, etc., especially those in industries with time- sensitive shipments (e.g., ecommerce or healthcare).
Check the consignment’s current status using online tracking tools and ensure that it is updated regularly.
Confirm whether the consignment is progressing and whether the event milestones have been reached as per schedule.
Check the reason for the delayed consignment at a transit hub and when the shipment will move, and file a complaint if necessary.
Confirm the updated last transit point and contact the concerned hub to find out the status in case of delay.
Follow up regularly with the concerned transportation/ carrier/ handler/ delivery centre department regarding the shipment’s current status and match that with the online tracking.
Update the client regularly about the shipment status and provide additional information about any changes in the transit time, contingencies, etc.
Identify and assess potential risks that could threaten the relationship, such as industry downturns, market changes, or internal issues at the client’s end.

Proactively look for potential issues affecting key clients’ experiences (e.g., shipping volume spikes due to holiday seasons or product launches) and prepare in advance to handle the increased demand.
Create contingency plans for delays, supply chain disruptions, or unexpected problems.
Establish a clear escalation process for handling issues or disputes.
Acknowledge the problem once raised by the customer and apologise for any inconvenience.
Request Detailed Information, perform basic checks, and provide a timeline for resolution.
Investigate the complaint and perform Root Cause analysis if required.
Propose an Effective Solution tailored to the specific complaint and the client’s expectations, e.g. Compensation or Reshipment for lost/ damaged goods.
Offer alternative solutions such as discounts or credit if the client’s preferred solution is impossible.
Keep the client updated throughout the resolution process.
Ensure that the agreed-upon solution is documented and timely action is taken.
Improve processes by implementing changes in procedures, whether that involves improving packaging standards, refining communication channels, or training staff in better handling practices.
Confirm with the client once the issue has been resolved to ensure they are satisfied with the outcome and the resolution.
Assist the client in processing an insurance claim for reimbursement if the shipment was insured.

pcs.pc_description: Gather the details of the shipment from the customer, including SLI (Shipper’s Letter of Instruction), packing list, certificate of origin, commercial invoice, customs approval to export (let export) and other relevant documents where appropriate.
Ensure that the shipment is permitted to be carried out without any restrictions or limitations and securely packed for carriage and destination norms.
Make a booking for pickup of consignments with appropriate codes, destination, shipment details, weight, dimensions, content, etc. and the requested timeslot in the booking software.
Communicate the expected pickup time, ETA, and any potential delays or factors that might affect the delivery schedule, customs clearance process at the origin and destination, etc.
Advise of any additional documentation required for customs purposes and issue an AWB (Airway Bill) copy to the customer once the shipment is picked up.

modules.module_title: Cross-Selling and Up-Selling for Key Consignors

pcs.pc_description: Analyse data on consignor sales volume, market trends, and seasonal demand fluctuations to forecast future sales and identify areas where improvements can be made (e.g., reducing return rates or increasing sales volume).
Identify areas where the consignor may need additional support or services, such as inventory management, logistics, customer service, or even marketing issues.
Categorise the customer needs based on volume, product types, or growth potential to offer more targeted cross-sell and up-sell opportunities.

Identify upselling opportunities and offer higher-value, premium versions of the consignor’s current products. For example, if the consignor regularly consigns a certain volume of goods, suggest increasing their order size to receive better pricing or offer bulk deals on complementary products.
Offer demonstrations or samples during a new service or product trial period.
Provide personalised consultations or business reviews to discuss other products or services that could benefit the consignor.

Set up automated reporting for key data points (e.g., weekly sales, stock updates, pending payments) and relevant external systems that can be sent directly to consignors, internal teams, and managers. For up-to-date tracking and reporting, set up real-time syncing between the MIS and relevant external systems (such as third-party logistics providers or financial institutions).
Implement features for analysing historical sales data and forecasting future demand, allowing the consignor to adjust inventory and marketing strategies accordingly.
Ensure the MIS supports seamless order processing and tracking, from initial order creation through delivery and post-delivery returns.
Set Up Automated Financial and Payment Tracking Alerts & Notifications based on consignment agreements, containing sales thresholds met, outstanding balances, payment due dates, etc.
Train key stakeholders, including consignors, internal teams, and managers, to ensure they understand how to use the MIS effectively.
Ensure the MIS system complies with relevant industry regulations (e.g., tax laws, trade regulations, or customs documentation).
Implement strong data security measures, such as encryption, access control, and regular security audits, to protect sensitive information, like sales data, payment details, or inventory levels.

pcs.pc_description: Analyse the client’s project requirements and assess the specific cargo characteristics (size, weight, fragility, etc.).
Collaborate with internal teams to identify the best transportation routes, modes of transport (road, rail, sea, air), and any special equipment needed (cranes, heavy-lift trailers, etc.).
Create and manage detailed project timelines, ensuring all shipments are timely, including any time-sensitive deliveries or critical milestones.
Maintain regular communication to update the client on the status of shipments, any issues, and progress toward deadlines.
Quickly address any challenges (such as customs issues, delays, or unforeseen complications) and inform the client of solutions.
Manage the transportation of goods closely with third-party logistics providers, freight forwarders, shipping lines, and handling companies.
Ensure all relevant documentation (shipping manifests, customs paperwork, permits, etc.) is prepared, accurate, and complies with international trade regulations.
Identify and mitigate potential risks of transporting high-value or sensitive cargo, including insurance, security, and handling concerns.
Verify compliance with all international, national, and local regulations for importing and exporting goods, including customs clearance, permits, and tariffs.
Confirm the necessary heavy-lift equipment, cranes, or special handling tools are available and coordinated for the cargo.
Arrange temporary warehousing or storage solutions before shipment or upon arrival, If necessary.
Continuously track shipments’ progress from origin to the final destination in real-time and provide regular status reports to the client, highlighting key milestones, challenges, and solutions.
Ensure the project cargo is delivered to the correct location and seek client feedback to improve future project handling.
Collect the photos and inform the relevant hub to examine the extent if a shipment is updated as damaged in transit.
Inform the customer and get his consent to repack if the packaging is damaged and the shipment’s contents are intact.
If the shipper/ consignee is not fine with further connecting the repacked shipment, coordinate to have it returned to its origin or stored until further instruction.
Coordinate with the customer for further instructions/ repair/ return/ scrap, etc., if the entire shipment, including its contents, is damaged.
Follow the lost shipment process if the status is not updated for more than 24 hours.
Initiate the searching process and check with the last updated hub for status updates.

Check manually with the transit hubs for the shipment’s status, and if the shipment has left a transit hub and has not reached the next hub/ station, track it with transport equipment identifiers (e.g., shipping container number/ULD/rail car IDs).

Start the manual searching process if the shipment is still untraceable with the master tracking IDs, and coordinate with the ground-level staff, such as drivers, loaders, cargo handlers at transhipment hubs, etc.
Check for CCTV footage, lost and found hub, unlabeled shipments, etc., as per the SOP set up with the carriers.
Verify with the consignee whether the shipment is delivered or reached the destination without updating the tracking details.
If the shipment is declared lost, File for insurance or claim according to the SOP signed with the carrier and perform root cause analysis if required.
Consider a shipment under transit delay if it does not move as scheduled and eventually affects or postpones the ETA.

Investigate with the carrier why the shipment has not moved as planned and whether the reason is due to negligence by the carrier/ handler, e.g., lack of loaders/ MHE, space constraints due to failed bookings, infrastructure failures, etc.
Escalate the situation according to the SOP/ matrix received from the carrier and file for a claim if required.
Ensure that the shipment is connected through the next possible connection.

If the shipment is delayed due to uncontrollable scenarios from the customs end, like physical inspection, congestion at the port, change of officers, revision of acts, etc., keep the shipper, consignee, and other stakeholders informed.
Plan the next connection according to the anticipated clearance date and inform the next carrier.

Check with the transit hub/ handler for safe storage of the shipment and the cost for the same; if the transit is delayed due to unforeseen circumstances like natural disasters, War/ like operations, technical failures/ vehicle breakdowns/ epidemics, strikes, government directions or force majeure, etc.,
Coordinate with the shipper, consignee/ stakeholders, etc., regarding the next action plan if the delay is more than anticipated and the situation remains unclear.

If the shipment is delayed due to Accidents, road construction, inclement weather enroute, road debris, rush hour congestion, etc., check with the carrier on the next plan for compensating the loss of transit time and update the stakeholders accordingly.
